topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Slope vs. Area
lecture_lines: Calculus links slope and area together.
animations: Draw linear function y = mx + b. Label slope m. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Highlight tangent line slope at a point x. (Color: #FFFF00)
Draw rectangle under curve, representing area. (Color: #00FFFF)
Increase rectangle width to approximate area better. (Color: #00FFFF)
Show area accumulation as width approaches zero. (Color: #00FF00)

sections.title: The Conceptual Inverse: Undo-ing the Action
lecture_lines: Differentiation and integration are inverse processes.
Think of them like addition and subtraction.
animations: Start with a block representing function f(x). (Color: #FFFFFF)
Show operator box 'D' transforming f to f'. (Color: #FF00FF)
Show operator box 'I' reversing f' back to f. (Color: #FF00FF)

sections.title: Visualizing the Fundamental Theorem
lecture_lines: Consider an accumulation function, A of x.
It represents area under f of t.
Increasing x adds a tiny rectangular slice.
The slice height is f of x.
Therefore, A prime is f of x.
animations: Display the curve f(t) and interval [a, x]. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Fill area under f(t) with translucent shade. (Color: #00FF00)
Slide right boundary x, showing area accumulation F(x). (Color: #FFFF00)

sections.title: Application: From Rate to Reality
lecture_lines: Rates of change reveal original states.
Integrals recover the position from acceleration.
This solves complex real-world physical problems.
animations: Graph a rate function v(t) over time. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Shade area under v(t) to show total displacement. (Color: #00FF00)
Animate displacement value increasing on the side. (Color: #FFFF00)
